title: Pieter Battier to Gaspar Fagel, Madrid, 1686–1688

plaintext.source: Scan 32R: numbered list 1–4 in a contemporary clerk's hand; four passages, 186 cipher tokens. Third validation letter, not a new reading. Confirms 15:325 = wat and 12:409 = syn (legacy C). On 31R L05, tokens 57–59 read 8:721 niet, 4:294 gedaan, 4:696 en, with no separate af prefix token; the clerk has niet afgedaen. A missing transcription token cannot be excluded without checking the cipher line against the image.

system.summary: A Dutch homophonic letter table accompanies an alphabetical codebook with fifteen marked number series and names.

diacritics.note: Fifteen blocks selected by overhead marks or struck digit; see NOTES.md.

system.notes: 1417 is the merged count (1393 earlier codes plus 24 new codes in 27 additional rows) of distinct transcribed dictionary codes, not the full historical codebook. Letter table 2–98; main blocks 99–999; names on key scans 59 and 78–82.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on inv. 401 scans 28R, 32R (19 December 1686, four numbered passages), 42R–43R and 101R; no edition found in the prior-art search.

conditions.human_role: Decipherment by Feyseel Nur with Claude and Codex; original division of transcription work undocumented.

solution.what: De Leeuw 2000 describes Fagel codebooks, not Battier; no edition found; letters absent from DECODE.
Named Battier key NA 1.10.29 inv. 1209, DECODE R2794; old 5345 citation corrected.
Letter table and about 1400 codebook values transcribed; marked cipher tokens and inventory retained.
Key applied to five focus letters and supporting letters; the earlier volume estimate was roughly 55%, with no revised denominator for the 235-token addition.

First two validation letters: 1113/1132 comparable tokens agree (98.3%); 94.7% key-alone; 18 positions not comparable. Third validation: 19 December 1686, four passages and 186 tokens, reproduces the contemporary list on 32R apart from spelling and gedaan/afgedaen. Confirms 15:325 = wat and 12:409 = syn; strengthens the identification of inv. 1209 as Battier's key. Comparison is not blind.
300-permutation control: 72% spelled runs segment into Dutch, mean 1.2%, maximum 4.1% shuffled.

Codex software re-decoding, not paleography: 19 Dec 186/186 is validation of contemporary plaintext; 24 April 1687 passes strict sense without a known contemporary decipherment, 230/235 (97.9%), as does 8 April 1688, 313/323 (96.9%), conservatively 312/323 (96.6%). Dec 1687 94.3% and Feb 1688 92.3% do not pass.

outcome.method_basis: The contemporary key explicitly names Battier; NA 1.10.29 inv. 1209 / DECODE R2794 was applied to his correspondence. The third validation against scan 32R strengthens this identification.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Earlier volume estimate, about 55% of cipher in inv. 401; no revised volume-wide denominator after adding 235 tokens from 24 April 1687. Inventory: inv/orch_letters.tsv and inv/nw.tsv. Strict results: codex_review/metrics.tsv and codex_review/review_1687-04-24.md.

gaps.detail: Surplus 8=e (possible encipherment slip); 5:623 gra[tie] partly covered in the key; gehelyk, sedert dat and soo als hy; exact condition of Gastanaga's departure. Five excluded positions: codex_review/review_1687-04-24.md.
12:6?0; getwist versus Turck(en); Novelli/Hofmeester; gesoubconneert gouverneren; Sex.; names, 81 and other repairs: codex_review/semantic_adjustments.tsv.

outcome.notes: Two letters pass strict sense without a known contemporary decipherment: 24 April 1687, 230/235 (97.9%) conservatively; 8 April 1688, 313/323 (96.9%), conservatively 312/323 (96.6%). The 19 December 1686 letter, 186/186, is the third validation against contemporary plaintext on 32R, not a new reading. Others 199/211 and 250/271 are below. No aggregate grade conversion or volume-wide coherent fraction is claimed. Legacy reading grades remain unchanged; 12:409 = syn is now confirmed by contemporary plaintext. 81=e is contextual and absent from all three validation letters.
